answer:
RMSNorm divides by √(mean(x²)+eps), then applies a learned scale; it does not subtract the feature mean. Accumulating the second moment in float32 reduces low-precision error. The implementation supports a scale initialized to one and a zero-centered parameterization using 1+weight. These are parameterization choices, not a guarantee that arbitrary model checkpoints are interchangeable.

**Mathematical and practical explanation.** $y_i=\gamma_i x_i/\sqrt{d^{-1}\sum_jx_j^2+\epsilon}$. This preserves the direction of a row before learned coordinate scaling, whereas centering in LayerNorm also changes that direction. Epsilon prevents division by zero but means exact scale invariance holds only approximately when the second moment dominates epsilon. [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1910.07467)

For the implementation or system context discussed above, see [1](https://sebastianraschka.com/faq/docs/rmsnorm-vs-layernorm.html) and [2](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.RMSNorm.html).
